Effective penalty of the ridge precision estimator

Source: R/ridgegraph.R
effective_penalty.Rd

Estimates the effective penalty \(\kappa = \lambda (1 + \delta)\) of the ridge precision estimator through the degrees-of-freedom ratio \(\hat r = \mathrm{tr}\{S (S + \lambda I)^{-1}\} / (n - 1)\), as \(\hat\kappa = \lambda / (1 - \hat r)\); returns the limit of \(\hat\kappa\) as \(\lambda \to 0\); and finds the penalty that attains a prescribed effective penalty. The columns of x are centred and \(S = X^\top X / (n - 1)\), so the effective sample size in all formulas is \(n - 1\), where \(n\) is the number of rows.

Usage

effective_penalty(x, lambda)

effective_penalty_floor(x, tol = 1e-10)

penalty_for_kappa(x, kappa)

Arguments

x

numeric data matrix with observations in rows.

lambda

vector of positive penalties.

tol

relative tolerance below which an eigenvalue of \(S\) is treated as zero.

kappa

target effective penalty, larger than effective_penalty_floor(x).

Value

effective_penalty returns a data frame with columns lambda, df_ratio (\(\hat r\)), scale (\(1 - \hat r\), an estimate of \(1 / (1 + \delta)\)) and kappa. effective_penalty_floor returns the harmonic mean of the positive eigenvalues of \(S\) when their number equals the effective sample size, and zero otherwise. penalty_for_kappa returns a penalty.

Details

The estimated effective penalty is continuous and strictly increasing in \(\lambda\), so penalty_for_kappa has a unique solution.

References

Arashi, M. and Ebrahim, E. K. (2026). What does a ridge network estimate? Effective penalty and leakage in ridge precision matrix estimation. Submitted.

Examples

set.seed(1)
x <- matrix(rnorm(30 * 60), 30, 60)
effective_penalty(x, c(0.01, 0.1, 1))
#>   lambda  df_ratio       scale    kappa
#> 1   0.01 0.9914974 0.008502633 1.176106
#> 2   0.10 0.9246945 0.075305543 1.327923
#> 3   1.00 0.6074250 0.392575010 2.547284
effective_penalty_floor(x)
#> [1] 1.15844
